findings.title: Human API errors now insert `[code]` into the established prefix
findings.evidence: At native/crates/agent-cli-core/src/lib.rs:218-229, the new human path formats `API error {status} [{code}]: ...`; the exact prior candidate at 5fd4c12 formatted `API error {status}: ...`. The new test at native/bins/rudder-cli/tests/member_directory.rs:219-225 asserts the changed format. The spec requires existing CLI output semantics to remain preserved.
findings.impact: This changes human stderr even for ordinary, control-free errors, and breaks consumers/operators matching the prior `API error <status>:` prefix. Escaping untrusted text requires a rendering change only when input contains control characters; it does not require adding the code field to the human format.
findings.smallest_resolution: Keep the prior human prefix and field layout while applying terminal escaping to the prior message/details fields. Omit the newly inserted code from human output; retain the code unchanged in JSON. Update the executable regression to assert both inert escaping and the preserved ordinary error format. No broader CLI or error-model redesign is needed.
